ld_description: Lightweight, free and open-source screen recorder for Windows and Linux, made for low-end PCs. It records the screen or a window, desktop audio and microphone to H.264 MP4 with the GPU's hardware encoder, with an interface that follows OBS Studio.
h1: The lightweight screen recorder for low-end PCs.
lead: Obs Lite records your screen, desktop audio and microphone to MP4 with your graphics card's hardware encoder. It looks and works like OBS Studio, in a {{MSI_SIZE}} download that leaves your game or app the CPU and memory it needs.
note_mac: Obs Lite is for Windows and Linux; there is no macOS version.
note_mobile: Obs Lite is a desktop app for Windows and Linux. Open this page on your PC to download it.

next_msi_3: Open Obs Lite from the Start menu and press Start Recording.

next_zip_2: Run obs-lite.exe. If Windows says “Windows protected your PC”, click More info, then Run anyway.

ro_zero: ads, accounts, watermarks or time limits

why_title: Light by design, not by settings.
why_lead: You can spend an evening tuning OBS Studio so an old laptop keeps up. Or you can use a recorder built from the start to stay out of the way of the game or app you are recording.
why1_t: Your GPU does the heavy lifting
why1_p: Video is encoded to H.264 by the graphics card's hardware encoder: NVIDIA NVENC, Intel Quick Sync, AMD AMF, or VA-API on Linux. On Windows, and with VA-API on Linux, each frame stays on the GPU from capture to encoder.
why2_p: On Windows, the screen is captured only when the image changes; Obs Lite repeats the last frame to keep a constant frame rate, so your video editor gets clean 30 or 60 fps.
why3_p: Obs Lite is a native program written in Rust, with no bundled browser engine: a {{MSI_SIZE}} installer that installs a single ~7 MB .exe on Windows, and a ~4 MB Flatpak on Linux.
why4_p: No streaming, scenes or plugins to load. What it leaves out is what keeps it small, and what makes it simple to use.
cmp_lead: Both on the same laptop under Linux, showing and then recording the whole screen with its audio, encoding with VA-API on the Intel GPU. Shorter is lighter.
cmp_note: While recording, OBS Studio uses a little less CPU; Obs Lite uses less memory and a fraction of the disk. Sizes: OBS Studio 33.0 from Flathub and Obs Lite 0.5.0 on the same runtime, measured with flatpak info on 2026-10-27. Memory and CPU: 2026-10-29, at 12 Mbit/s with a keyframe every 2 s. Details in the README.

feat_title: Everything you need to record. Nothing you don't.
feat_lead: The recording tools people use every day in OBS Studio, with OBS's own wording, so you find everything where you expect it.
f1_p: Record a whole display or a single window, with or without the cursor, or drag a rectangle on the preview to record only part of it.
f2_p: MP4 files at a constant 30 or 60 fps that open in every player and video editor, scaled on the GPU to 1440p, 1080p or 720p if you like.
f3_p: Mixed together, each with its own meter, volume and mute button. Mute works in the middle of a recording.
f4_p: Record a game's sound without your Discord call: Application Audio Capture gives one program its own mixer channel.
f5_p: Keeps the last seconds in memory, already encoded. Press Save Replay to keep a moment that already happened.
f6_p: If the PC crashes or loses power, the recording is kept, and turned into a regular MP4 the next time Obs Lite starts.
f7_p: Show your webcam on the recording. Drag it on the preview to move it, or its corner to resize it.
f8_p: Removes fan hum and keyboard clatter from the microphone, with the same filter OBS Studio offers.
f9_p: Start, stop, pause, save a replay, take a screenshot or mute the mic from inside any game or app.
f10_p: Paused time never reaches the file, in video or in audio.
f11_p: The Obs Lite window never shows up in your recordings or in its own preview.
f12_p: Follows your system's language. Plus a system tray icon, screenshots and one-click updates for the installed version.
start_lead: No account, no setup wizard, no settings to tune first.
s1_p: Run the installer: no administrator rights needed. Or unzip the portable version anywhere. On Linux, install the Flatpak.
s2_p: Press Start Recording, or Ctrl+Alt+R from anywhere. It records your main display and desktop audio at 60 fps.
s3_p: Your MP4 is in the Videos folder, named after the time it started. File › Show Recordings opens it.
callout_1: Windows may show “Windows protected your PC” the first time. Obs Lite is signed with OpenPGP instead of a paid Windows code-signing certificate, so SmartScreen does not recognise it yet. Click More info, then Run anyway.
callout_2: Every file has a PGP signature and a GitHub build attestation, so you can check it is genuine. The source code is public on GitHub.
req_win_1: Windows 11, 64-bit. Windows 10 has not been tested yet.
req_win_2: A GPU with a working driver: NVIDIA, Intel or AMD. Without a hardware encoder, Windows' software encoder takes over (more CPU).
req_linux_2: A desktop with the screen-sharing portal: GNOME, KDE Plasma and most Wayland desktops. Works on Wayland and X11.
faq1_q: What is the best screen recorder for a low-end PC?
faq1_a: One that hands the encoding to the graphics card and carries nothing you don't use. Obs Lite was made for exactly that: it records with the GPU's hardware encoder (NVENC, Quick Sync, AMF or VA-API), is a {{MSI_SIZE}} download, and uses about 100 MB of memory with the preview running. It needs a GPU or integrated graphics with a working driver; most Intel, AMD and NVIDIA graphics from the last decade have a hardware H.264 encoder.
faq2_q: Is Obs Lite a lighter alternative to OBS Studio?
faq2_a: For recording, yes. Obs Lite has the same layout as OBS Studio (preview, Sources, Audio Mixer, Controls) and uses OBS's wording, but it only records: no streaming, scenes or plugins. In exchange, its Flatpak is {{N:3.7}} MB against 225 MB, and it uses less memory. If you stream or build scenes, OBS Studio is the right tool.
faq3_q: Is Obs Lite made by the OBS Project?
faq3_a: No. Obs Lite is an independent project, written from scratch in Rust. It contains no OBS code and is not affiliated with, endorsed by or sponsored by the OBS Project. It follows OBS Studio's interface so that OBS users feel at home.
faq4_a: Yes. Obs Lite is free and open source under the MIT license: no ads, no account, no watermark and no time limit on recordings.
faq5_q: Can I record a game without recording my Discord call?
faq5_a: Yes, on Windows. Add an Application Audio Capture source for the game: its sound gets its own channel in the mixer, and desktop audio leaves it out. Mute desktop audio, and the game is recorded without the call.
faq6_q: Why does Windows say “Windows protected your PC”?
faq6_a: Windows SmartScreen warns about programs that are not signed with a paid Windows code-signing certificate. Obs Lite is signed with OpenPGP instead, and every file comes with a GitHub build attestation that shows which commit it was built from. Click More info, then Run anyway.
faq7_q: What happens if my PC crashes while recording?
faq7_a: The recording is kept. Obs Lite writes the MP4 in small fragments, so after a crash or a power cut the file has everything but the last fraction of a second, and the next time Obs Lite starts it turns it into a regular MP4.
faq8_a: In your Videos folder, as MP4 files named after the time the recording started (for example 2026-10-16 13-45-02.mp4). You can change the folder in Settings › Output.
faq9_q: Does Obs Lite collect any data?
faq9_a: No. On Windows it only asks GitHub at start-up whether there is a newer version, and you can turn that off in Settings › General. The Linux Flatpak has no network access at all.
faq10_a: It has not been tested there yet. Obs Lite is built and tested on Windows 11; if you try it on Windows 10, a report on GitHub is very welcome.
cta_p: Download Obs Lite for free and start recording in under a minute.
